name: Count Subrectangles
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ both consisting of only integers $$$0$$$ and $$$1$$$. Consider a matrix $$$c$$$ of size $$$n \times m$$$ formed by following rule: $$$c_{i, j} = a_i \cdot b_j$$$ (i.e. $$$a_i$$$ multiplied by $$$b_j$$$). It's easy to see that $$$c$$$ consists of only zeroes and ones too. How many subrectangles of size (area) $$$k$$$ consisting only of ones are there in $$$c$$$? A subrectangle is an intersection of a consecutive (subsequent) segment of rows and a consecutive (subsequent) segment of columns. I.e. consider four integers $$$x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2$$$ ($$$1 \le x_1 \le x_2 \le n$$$, $$$1 \le y_1 \le y_2 \le m$$$) a subrectangle $$$c[x_1 \dots x_2][y_1 \dots y_2]$$$ is an intersection of the rows $$$x_1, x_1+1, x_1+2, \dots, x_2$$$ and the columns $$$y_1, y_1+1, y_1+2, \dots, y_2$$$. The size (area) of a subrectangle is the total number of cells in it.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, m \leq 40\,000, 1 \leq k \leq n \cdot m$$$), length of array $$$a$$$, length of array $$$b$$$ and required size of subrectangles. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \leq 1$$$), elements of $$$a$$$. The third line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m$$$ ($$$0 \leq b_i \leq 1$$$), elements of $$$b$$$.
output_specification: Output single integer — the number of subrectangles of $$$c$$$ with size (area) $$$k$$$ consisting only of ones.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1323B — Count Subrectangles [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
